body:
Rafael Mendes: Dropping post-game-day findings here so we don’t lose them. Please reply w/ anything I missed + add owners if you can. Goal is to convert to follow-up tickets by EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Reminder: game day notes doc updated by @Rafael Mendes. (internal link) https://go.redwoodinference.com/docs/game-day/auto-rollback-2026-02

Sean Gallagher: +1. Biggest theme for me: we still have a lot of “monitor missing/stale” cases and our current behavior is inconsistent across services (some fail-open, some effectively fail-closed).

Aisha Bello: Agree. During scenario #2 (5xx burst) the evaluator queried burn-rate OK, but for latency we got `no_data` for p99 in eu-west for ~4m and we treated it as “healthy” and continued step. That’s a false negative.

Jada Williams: For clarity, controller currently does: if monitor adapter returns `stale=true` -> suppress auto-action + record outcome “monitor_stale”. But if adapter returns “no monitor id configured” we treat as `skip` and continue. That’s what happened for the p99 eu-west route (policy had latency p95 configured, not p99).

Allison Grant: That’s a policy UX problem too. In Console policy editor, we allow picking “latency” but don’t force percentile selection, so folks assume p99 is included. We should either (a) make it explicit (p95 vs p99) or (b) ship a default pair.

Chloe Martin: +1, UI shows “Latency SLO” without the details unless you click the advanced drawer. We should at least show `p95` / `p99` chips in the summary.

Rafael Mendes: Findings bucket 1: false positives / flapping
- In low-volume canary steps (1% traffic), we tripped error-rate burn fast window on 6 total requests (1 5xx) and paused. That’s “correct” per math but not what we want operationally.

Sean Gallagher: Yep. Need min sample gating on BOTH windows. Right now min sample is applied only to slow window (30m) per config default, but fast window (5m) can still trigger on tiny N. We talked about min requests >= 200 (or per-tier) before allowing any action.

Jordan Lee: Confirmed. The `minRequests` check is only tied to `slowWindowStatus`, not `fastWindowStatus`. Easy change but needs ADR alignment.

Priya Natarajan: Let’s just do it. If we want to keep ultra-sensitive behavior, it should be an opt-in (advanced config), not default.

Aisha Bello: Also: we had flapping when latency was oscillating around threshold and we did pause -> resume -> pause. Debounce exists but resets when step changes. So a rollout step transition can clear history and we re-trigger.

Jada Williams: That’s on us. Debounce key currently is `(rollout_id, step_id, monitor_id)`. When step_id increments, we lose holdoff state. We need debounce keyed at least at rollout scope (and maybe action type) so “fast burn” doesn’t re-fire immediately post transition.

Rafael Mendes: Findings bucket 2: missing monitors / staleness
- Missing p99 monitors for: `chat.completions` route in eu-west (hosted) + a couple dedicated tenant routes (names redacted in this thread, in doc)
- Stale data detection: adapter marks stale if last datapoint > 180s old, but telemetry pipeline lag was ~210-240s during the game day load. So we suppressed actions even though SLO was legitimately bad.

Logan Wright: Re telemetry lag: we saw batching changes in staging causing Mimir ingest backpressure. We can probably keep lag < 120s with config, but we should not assume 180s always safe.

Allison Grant: From observability standards POV: “stale” threshold must be tied to monitor eval window. If your fast window is 5m, a 3-4m lag might still be usable but you need to treat it as “degraded confidence”, not just suppress.

Sean Gallagher: I’d rather we do: if stale AND we’re in active rollout -> default action is “pause” (safe) rather than “continue”. Continuing while blind is worse for us.

Benji Okafor: That’s a policy decision. We can add `onMissingMonitor` + `onStaleMonitor` behavior fields in policy engine with safe defaults. Proposed:
- missing monitor: pause rollout (not rollback)
- stale monitor: pause rollout + alert
- monitor provider unavailable: pause rollout + alert
We can gate by tier (self-serve vs dedicated) but default should be conservative.

Connor O'Brien: Release gating angle: we should block enabling auto-rollback for a service/model unless required monitors exist in all enabled regions. That’s literally what bit us here.

Leila Farouk: For E2E, we need deterministic tests for “missing monitor pauses” vs “stale monitor pauses” and ensure audit trail includes the reason. Right now tests only check pause on SLO breach.

Felix Schneider: Findings bucket 3: audit trail + “why did we rollback” UX
- Event contains monitor id + decision, but doesn’t include *which labels/scope* were evaluated (route/model_version/region/tier) in a human-readable way.
- Metrics snapshot link in event is sometimes empty because we didn’t generate the dashboard URL for dedicated tenant scopes.

Chloe Martin: In Console we can render the scope string from rollout object (we have route + model version + regions), but we should still store it in the audit event so it’s immutable.

Aisha Bello: Also need to store policy version/hash. We had someone ask “did we change defaults mid-game-day?” and we had to dig through config history.

Jordan Lee: Policy engine can include `policy_revision` and `effective_at` in the returned evaluated policy. We just need to thread it through the event emitter.

Rafael Mendes: Findings bucket 4: alerting / noise
- Auto-pause fired 7 times across scenarios, incident-bot posted 7 times, but no aggregation so channel got spammy.
- For “suppressed due to incident” case, we didn’t post anything (by design) and oncall missed that we were running blind.

Sean Gallagher: We should differentiate:
1) Auto action taken (pause/rollback) -> notify + page depending on tier
2) Auto action suppressed (incident override) -> notify (no page) w/ reason
3) Auto action skipped due to monitor missing/stale -> notify service owner + SRE (no page) because it’s actionable hygiene

Allison Grant: +1 but please keep label cardinality under control. If we tag rollout_id in alert labels we’ll explode alert instances. Better: include rollout_id in annotation/body, not labels.

Caleb Johnson: On metrics side: we currently label `rollout_id` on `rollout_slo_eval_total` (counter). That’s going to be a cardinality nightmare in prod. We should move rollout_id to logs/events only and keep metrics aggregated by service/route/model_version maybe.

Jada Williams: Agree. We added rollout_id to make debugging easier but it’s not sustainable. We can keep `rollout_hash` or `rollout_policy_template` maybe, and rely on audit events for rollouts.

Rafael Mendes: Ok, action items draft (reply w/ corrections / owners):
1) Min sample gating for fast window + slow window; default minRequests per tier (self-serve higher?) — Owner: Jordan + Sean
2) Debounce/holdoff state should persist across rollout step transitions — Owner: Jada
3) Policy additions: `onMissingMonitor`, `onStaleMonitor`, `onMonitorProviderError` with safe defaults (pause + alert), plus UI exposure — Owner: Benji + Chloe
4) Release gate: require monitor coverage for enabled regions/tiers before enabling auto-rollback; add checklist + automation — Owner: Connor + Aisha
5) Audit trail: include evaluated scope summary + policy revision/hash + dashboard URL generation for dedicated scopes — Owner: Felix
6) Alerting: add notifications for suppressed/skipped; reduce spam via grouping; ensure no paging storm — Owner: Aisha + Sean
7) Metrics: remove rollout_id label from high-volume metrics; confirm updated naming/labels align with standards — Owner: Caleb + Allison
8) E2E tests: add missing monitor + stale monitor scenarios; assert audit reason + UI surfaces correctly — Owner: Leila

Connor O'Brien: For #4, I can add it to ENG-4850 release plan and create a release gate doc. We’ll likely need a “monitor coverage audit” job to run in CI for new routes/models.

Aisha Bello: I’ll take #6 but need someone from incident-bot side to implement grouping. Maybe we can do “1 msg per rollout per 10m” unless severity changes.

Sean Gallagher: I’ll coordinate. For paging: only rollback in prod dedicated/private should page service oncall; hosted self-serve should notify #eng-sre + #eng-platform only.

Benji Okafor: #3: I’ll draft schema changes. We should also set guardrails so customers can’t set `onMissingMonitor=continue` in prod unless admin override.

Priya Natarajan: Strong +1. Missing monitor should never mean “continue” for auto-rollback-enabled services. If customer wants that, they can disable auto-rollback.

Felix Schneider: For #5, I’ll update audit event fields. One more: add `decision_trace_id` so we can correlate evaluator logs + controller action + incident-bot message.

Jada Williams: Re #2: I’ll implement debounce store keyed by `(rollout_id, monitor_key)` and include step_id in the payload but not the key. Will also add “holdoff after action” so it doesn’t immediately trigger rollback after a pause/resume.

Allison Grant: For #7, please run proposed label changes by me before merge. We need to keep `model_version` label cardinality manageable too (bounded by pinned versions / not per-request).

Caleb Johnson: Yep. Suggest metrics labels: `service`, `route`, `region`, `tier`, `signal` (latency_p95, latency_p99, error_rate), `outcome` (healthy/breached/stale/missing/suppressed), `action` (none/pause/rollback). No rollout_id.

Leila Farouk: For #8, I’ll add staging harness toggles to inject:
- missing monitor (policy references non-existent id)
- stale data (freeze synthetic metrics for > threshold)
- provider error (simulate 503 from slo-toolkit)
And assert controller goes into PAUSED + audit event includes correct suppression/skip reason.

Rafael Mendes: Perfect. I’ll open follow-ups tomorrow morning and link them here. If anyone has additional “gotchas” drop them in-thread.

Sean Gallagher: One more gotcha: “known incident override” currently requires manual entry of incident id. During game day we fat-fingered it and suppression didn’t apply. We should validate incident ids and/or allow selecting from active incidents list.

Chloe Martin: That’s UI + API. We can add an autocomplete backed by incident service (read-only) and validation server-side.

Aisha Bello: + also: when suppression is active, show banner in rollout page (“Auto actions suppressed until <time> by <user> (reason)”) so people don’t assume it’s still protecting them.

Felix Schneider: Noted. That banner can come from audit events + current suppression state.

Rafael Mendes: Added. Thanks all.
